references.why: Chrysostom's loose paraphrase of the friends' charge (Zophar, Job 11:6); Segond's wording differs, so rendered from the source.
Chrysostom blends Luke 6:23 (rejoice and leap for joy) with Luke 6:22 (cast out your name as evil); built from Segond's phrases but blended.
Chrysostom's text reads 'the more … so much the more', a comparative Segond does not have; kept, with Segond's vocabulary.

Chrysostom quotes the Septuagint (Ps 80:17 LXX) as a past-tense narrative of the wilderness miracle, and his argument depends on it ('recounting the wonders'); Segond 81:17 is a first-person conditional ('je le rassasierais du miel du rocher'). Kept Segond's 'du miel du rocher'.
Chrysostom's paraphrase/inversion of Prov 27:7b ('that wise man'); no Segond wording carries it. Attribution to 27:7 is inferred — the source gives no citation.
Chrysostom quotes the Septuagint (« three days »); Segond has « quarante jours ». Kept the preacher's three days, which his argument uses; « et Ninive est détruite » follows Segond.
Septuagint-shaped wording (« every man », « converted to the Lord ») that Segond does not have.
Segond reads « jusqu’à moi »; Chrysostom's point is the height (« unto the heaven »), so his wording is kept.
Singular « every one » as the preacher quotes it; Segond has the plural « ils revenaient de leur mauvaise voie ».
The preacher's text adds « in Heaven » (Theodotion); Segond has « notre Dieu que nous servons ».
